retry_state.type: ReadStatus { Complete { record_type, len }, WouldBlock, Fatal, Eof, FatalEof, Failed }
retry_state.invariant: Only Complete carries a length; ssl3_read_bytes maps WouldBlock/Fatal/Failed -> -1 and Eof/FatalEof -> 0, preserving the authority's return values, but no error or retry value can be consumed as bytes.
retry_state.assembly: AssemblyStep { Deliver{off,len}, NeedMore{used}, Refuse } with rd_msg_len/rd_msg_off normalised against the buffer first; a completed empty handshake record is Complete{len:0}, skipped and the loop continues (MAX_EMPTY_RECORDS=32), instead of the pre-fix -1 retry.
retry_state.compatibility_note: A zero-length record now also reports its content type (authority assigns *recvd_type before its len==0 arm); the return value remains 0.

buffer_ownership.inline: rec_hdr, rec_body and rd_msg_buf are inline fields of Ssl. The Ssl block is the single owner; their lifecycle is the connection's and their single release is SSL_free (outside this file). No failure path frees, replaces or moves them; the test asserts address and extent identity across the overflow and invalid-alert paths.
buffer_ownership.heap: The write scratch has exactly one owner per write (Scratch, wrapping OwnedBuf at the ssl3_buffer.c:124 seam). Its Drop is the only release, on success and on every encoder/BIO failure return; observed by address in the test.
buffer_ownership.accumulators: rec_hdr_len/rec_body_len/rd_msg_len/rd_msg_off are re-validated against their buffers on every use; a stale or corrupted value is a refusal, never an out-of-range slice.

discharged: No typed slice is formed over caller-supplied writable memory; publication is bounded by OutBuf's written ledger.
A partial read is WouldBlock and never a Complete; a fatal/EOF outcome carries no length.
A completed zero-length handshake record no longer stalls assembly behind a retry (pre-fix failure recorded).
Every offset, capacity and subtraction on the path is checked; an out-of-range accumulator is refused.
The write scratch is released exactly once on every return path (RAII, observed by address).
The connection's inline record buffers are never freed, replaced or moved by a failure path (observed by address identity).
Both entry points now state the BIO-callback non-reentrancy precondition they already relied on.
retained: `&mut *s` is formed from the C ABI pointer: liveness/exclusive ownership is the caller's contract, not a type invariant.
OutBuf::from_raw's writable extent and non-overlap are caller obligations.
Sink::slot hands a raw writable region derived from the connection; the internal call structure (index, not pointer, crosses into read_record) is what prevents a second alias, not the type system.
BIO_read/BIO_write and the AEAD sinks require their own liveness/extent contracts; the connection invariant covers them but a hostile in-crate `Ssl` construction could violate it.
The write scratch allocation-failure path is a plain -1; no failure-injection court was run (the allocator latch is one-way).
introduced: MAX_EMPTY_RECORDS=32 for consecutive empty handshake records: on exceeding it the reader returns -1 (no progress) instead of the authority's fatal SSL_R_RECORD_TOO_SMALL, to avoid adding a new error coordinate in this batch. Recorded as a deliberate divergence.

compatibility_delta: No intended change to the TLS 1.2 and 1.3 record formats, short-read/WANT_READ behaviour, alert handling, AEAD tag path, error codes or coordinates. Two deliberate, documented deltas: (1) a completed zero-length record now reports recvd_type (return stays 0), matching the authority; (2) a completed empty handshake record no longer returns -1 from the assembly reader (it is skipped, as tls_common.c does). Divergence from the authority: MAX_EMPTY_RECORDS exhaustion returns -1 rather than raising SSL_R_RECORD_TOO_SMALL.

The BIO-callback non-reentrancy obligation is external: a custom BIO method that re-enters this connection would invalidate the `&mut Ssl`. It is now stated on every entry point (it was implicit before).
residuals.disposition: Documented caller obligation; the authority makes the same assumption. Not type-enforceable at the C ABI.

residuals.disposition: Release is by RAII over a single owner, so the property is structural; allocation-failure injection NOT_RUN.
